contexts.story: Open by reframing career growth in the AI/LLM era: the ground is shifting fast, so the real risk is standing still, not moving. Use Chao’s journey as a quick proof that roles and required skills can change dramatically within a single career.
Contrast the old, linear model of AI/product work with today’s LLM-centric reality to show why traditional career playbooks are no longer enough and why adaptability is now a core career skill.
Introduce the first pillar of modern career growth: evolve with the industry by embracing new ways of working (like orchestration and UX focus) and accepting that role boundaries will blur.
Shift to the second pillar: focus on high-ROI work—defining the right problems, building feedback loops, and combining domains—because that’s where leverage and visibility now come from.
Offer concrete, step-by-step practices for doing high-value work in the LLM era: define problems well, tune prompts pragmatically, and design systems that limit error accumulation.
Highlight enduring human advantages—system-level thinking and low-level performance skills—and use Chao’s optimization anecdote to show how local brilliance can still fail without the right scope.
Address the fear of being left behind by showing how roles historically merged (like manual testers) and how you can stay current with AI through lightweight, sustainable habits.
Close with a simple career operating system: make every step solid and keep moving with the industry, turning daily tasks into compounding skill and opportunity.
